newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgutneftegaz signs ADR deal with bank.
newsitem.headline: Surgutneftegaz signs ADR deal with bank.

text.p: Russian oil company OAO Surgutneftegaz has signed a depositary agreement with The Bank of New York as part of plans to issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), its holding company said on Monday.
NK Surgutneftegaz (Surgut Holding) said in a statement the oil company had reached the final stages of preparations for an issue of level-one ADRs on its ordinary shares.

The company's board of directors had sent an F-6 form, an official application for an issue, to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The SEC should examine the form by December 1, the statement said.
ADRs allow U.S. investors to trade foreign shares without settlement and custody problems in the issuer's market.
Level one ADRs give investors access to a company's shares but do not raise new capital.
Surgutneftegaz said in May it planned to issue ADRs before the end of the year.

Russia's own securities watchdog, the Federal Commission for the Capital Markets, said earlier on Monday it was examining a supplementary share issue by Surgutneftegaz which was acquired in its entirety by Surgut Holding.
The commission said it was checking whether investors' rights had been violated and that it had asked the Finance Ministry to suspend the issue pending the results of the inquiry.
Surgutneftegaz stood at $0.425 on the Russian Trading System at 1340 GMT after closing on Sunday, a trading day, at $0.408
